caseno: Civil Revision No. 524 of 1990 with Civil Revision No.525 of 1990.
lawyer:
Syed Ziaul Karim, Advocate — For the Petitioner. 

Md Nurul Haque with AKM Shahidul Haque and Chamon Akhtar, Advocates — For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Siddique Ali Mia  ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Atahar Ali Fakir, being dead one of his heirs 1 (a) Abul Fakir &ors ------ Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
These two Rules arise out of Title Suit No. 539 of 1980 of the court of the then Munsif, Jhalakati and Title Suit No. 421 of 1977 of the same court. The petitioner is the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 539 of 1980 and the opposite party No. 1 is the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 421 of 1977 and the opposite party No. 1 is defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 539 of 1980 and the present petitioner is defendant No. 1 in Title Suit No. 421 of 1977. Both the suits were analogously heard by the learned Munsif and disposed of by him by one judgment. Similarly the appellate Court also heard the appeals analogously and disposed of the same by one judgment. Hence both the Rules were heard together and being disposed of by this judgment.

2. The petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 539 of 1980 before the court of .Munsif now Assistant Judge, Jhalakati for declaration that the certificate sale dated 15-1-63 in Certificate Sale case No. 1832-JK /1961-62 of the Sadar South Certificate Court of Barisal and Certificate Sale Case No. 1832-JK /1961-62 of the Sadar south at Barisal and certificate sale dated 30-11-63 in Certificate Sale Case No. 313 (JK) of Certificate Court at Jhalakati and the Certificate Sale dated 30-11-63 in Certificate Sale Case No. 6166 (JK) of Certificate Court at Jhalakati described in the schedule ''Ka'' of the plaint in respect or schedule "Kha" is illegal, fraudulent, collusive, inoperative without jurisdiction and not binding upon the plaintiff.

3. The case of the plaintiff, in short, is that "Kha" schedule land originally belonged to opposite party Nos.9-16 Sudhangshu Kumar and opposite party Nos.9-16 made a settlement of the above described land in favour of the plaintiff and opposite party Nos.17 and 18 on 20th Baisakh, 1358 BS. The plaintiff and opposite party Nos.17 and 18 after settlement created dwelling huts, planted fruit trees, constructed graveyard, cultivated the null land and paid rent on receipt of dakhilas and thus they had been continuing in the peaceful possession over the suit land. The settlement was made after RS operation and the State acquisition operation was not held in the locality and the record of SA Khatian was wrongly prepared as per RS khatian in the name of Shudhangshu Kumar and opposite party Nos.9-16. Thereafter the plaintiff petitioner and opposite party Nos.17 and 18 as plaintiffs filed a suit being numbered 339 of 1976 for declaration of their title over the suit land against Sudhangshu Kumar and opposite party Nos.9-16 before the court of Munsif at Jhalakati. The suit was decreed on compromise on 18-9-1976. The plaintiff petitioner and the opposite party Nos.17 and 18 on the basis of the decree dated 18-9-1976 filed Mutation Case No. 5-JK/ 1977-78 under section 54 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act before the Circle Officer (Revenue) Jhalakati and obtained an order of mutation and accordingly a new khatian being No. 801 was opened in their names and paid Government rent and obtained dakhilas for years together. It is stated in the plaint that the opposite party No. 1 is a greedy man of the locality and the opposite party Nos. 2-8 are his associates.

4. The opposite parties Nos. 1-8 knowing fully well about the right, title and interest of the petitioner and opposite party Nos.17 and 18 illegally and for wrongful gain managed to create the "ka" schedule certificate sale cases in respect of "Kha" schedule land of the plaint. It is further stated in the plaint that the certificate debtors of the "ka" schedule certificate cases were disinterested at the time of certificate sale, notices upon the opposite party Nos.9-16 were not served and the same was fraudulently shown to have been served, the certificate sale was illegal, without jurisdiction, fraudulent and were null and void. The petitioner and opposite parties Nos.17 and 18 being the legal owner of the land of the "Ka" schedule certificate cases were not made parties, the notices under sections 7 and 46 of the Public Demand Recovery Act were not at all served upon the certificate debtors, the "ka" schedule certificate sales remained confined in papers and it was not at all acted upon and therefore the physical possession was not delivered.

5. The opposite. party Nos. 1, 5, and 6 appeared in the said title suit on 10-6-1981, filed a joint written statement on the allegation, inter alia, that the suit was not maintainable and that suit was bad for defect of parties and the suit was barred by res judicata and the suit property was under-valued, the plaint was insufficiently stamped and the suit was barred by limitation and was not maintainable for want of cause of action. The opposite party Nos.9-16 were the legal owners and accordingly, for non-payment of Government rent the "ka" scheduled certificate cases were started and the same were legally and lawfully purchased by opposite party Nos.1-8. The story of the settlement of the petitioner was false. The petitioner at the time of alleged settlement was not a citizen of Pakistan and the father of the petitioner on 3-2-53 for the first time entered into Pakistan and that at the time of the alleged pattan the plaintiff was a boy of 2/3 years only and therefore the suit of the plaintiff-petitioner was liable to be dismissed.

6. The opposite party No. 1 as plaintiff earlier filed the Title Suit No. 421 of 1977 for setting aside the sole decree obtained by the petitioner and opposite party Nos.17-18. In that case present petitioner being defendant No. l contested the suit by filing written statement. The learned Munsif now Assistant Judge heard both the suits analogously and delivered one judgment for both the suits.

7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the aforesaid judgment, the plaintiff preferred an appeal before the learned District Judge, Jhalakati and the appeal was registered as Title Appeal No. 86 of 1986. Similarly, being aggrieved by the judgment of the trial Court the opposite party No. I preferred 2 appeals before the learned District Judge, Jhalakati which were registered as Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986 and 88 of 1986, The learned appellate Court below heard these 3 appeals analogously and disposed of by the impugned judgment whereby he dismissed Title Appeal No. 86 of 1986 and allowed Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986 by reversing the judgment of the trial Court and decreed Title Suit No. 421 of 1977. The present petitioner being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment and decree passed by the learned appellate Court below preferred Civil Revision No. 524 of 1990 calling in question the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below in Title Appeal No. 86 of 1986 and preferred Civil Revision No. 525 of 1990 against the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court below in Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986.

8. Mr Syed Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff appellant petitioner, submits that the trial Court found the petitioners in possession of the suit property but the learned appellate Court without reversing the finding of possession illegally dismissed the appeal and the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside. The learned Advocate submits that the trial Court observed that the claim of the contesting defendants was barred under section 66 of the Code of Civil Procedure, and found that the "ka" schedule certificate cases were fradulently created but the appellate Court below without reversing the finding of the trial Court illegally accepted the "ka" schedule certificate cases and thereby committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The learned Advocate further submits that both the courts below misdirected themselves in not considering the rent receipts filed by the plaintiff-petitioner as a genuine document of his possession and of his title and the learned Advocate submits that the courts below have committed an error of law in accepting the death certificate of Sudhangshu Kumar in evidence without calling the Death Register or without examining the authority concerned who granted the same. The learned Advocate further submits that in allowing the appeal No. 87 of 1988 the appellate Court lost sight of the fact that witnesses of the defendant opposite parties are highly interested and inter-related. The learned Advocate finally submits that in any view the impugned judgment is not tenable in law and the appellate Court below on misreading of evidence has dismissed Title Appeal No. 86 of 1988 and allowed title Appeal No. 87 of 1986.

9. Mrs Chamon Akhter, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No. 1, submits that the appellate Court below on proper scrutiny of materials on record rightly dismissed Title Appeal No. 86 of 1986 and allowed Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986. The learned Advocate further submits that the appellate Court below after considering the documentary evidence adduced by the defendant-opposite party No.  1 in their Title Suit No. 421 of 1977 rightly arrived at a finding that the defendant opposite party No. I has been able to prove his case and thereby rightly decreed the suit and allowed the appeal. The learned Advocate further submits that although the appellate Court below did not make any observation as to the interestedness and relationships of the witnesses of the defendant opposite party Nod nevertheless in view of the facts and circumstances of the case they are found to be most competent witnesses and their testimony cannot be thrown away on this ground alone. The learned Advocate further submits that since the defendant opposite party No. 1 is the real owner, section 66 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no manner of application in the instant suit.

<u>10. On a perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the appellate Court below on scrutiny of the materials on record found that the plaintiff-petitioner has failed to prove his case in respect of his title to the suit land and also found that he fraudulently, obtained decree in Title Suit No. 339 of 1976. It appears on persusal of the judgments of both the courts below that both the courts arrived at a concurrent findings of fact that the plaintiff petitioner could not prove his case. Although there is no elaborate discussion by the appellate Court with reference to the evidence adduced by the PWs in Title Suit No. 539 of 1980, nevertheless it appears that the findings arrived at by the appellate Court are based on material and evidence on record and the trial Court made elaborate discussions with reference to the materials on record and arrived at a positive findings that the defendant No. 1 of Title Suit No. 339 of 1976 died before the decree was passed in that suit. It is also found by the learned trial Court that the summons of Title Suit No. 339 of 1976 was not duly served on the defendant of that suit. The trial Court on a scrutiny of the evidence adduced by the plaintiff petitioner however, arrived at a finding that the plaintiff petitioner has failed to prove his title but he has found plaintiff petitioner in possession of the suit land. With this finding that trial Court dismissed the suit. Ziaul Karim, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner, submitted that the trial Court committed an illegality in taking into evidence the death certificate without calling for witnesses to prove the same. Besides, by oral evidence it has been proved that the defendant No. I of Title Suit No. 339 of 1976 died on 26-10-76. It further appears from the evidence of DW 4 that the plaintiff petitioner filed the aforesaid suit, after the death of Sudhangshu Kumar or after he left for India and taking into consideration all the evidence the trial Court arrived at a finding that the decree obtained by the plaintiff petitioner in Title Suit No. 339 of 1976 was fraudulent, void and inoperative. The learned appellate Court also found that the plaintiff petitioner has miserably failed to substantiate his contention that he took settlement from the original owner Sudhangshu Kumar, and others. Since both the courts have arrived at a concurrent finding based on the materials on record it is very difficult to interfere with such findings sitting under the revisional jurisdiction.</u>

11. Therefore, I do not find any substance in the submissions made by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner in respect of title Appeal No. 86 of 1986 and it appears to me that the appellate Court rightly dismissed the appeal and thereby he has not committed any illegality whatsoever. In that view of the matter the Rule in Civil Revision, No. 524 of 1990 is discharged without cost.

<u>12. On a perusal of the impugned judgment it appears that the learned appellate Court below on consideration of the materials on record and documentary evidence produced by the plaintiff in TS No. 421 of 1977 has arrived at a finding that the plaintiff has been able to prove his case and proved that they are in possession of the suit land in pursuance of the auction sale of the land held earlier. It may be mentioned that the trial Court considered this evidence and observed that although they filed these papers but there is not an iota of evidence adduced by the plaintiff to show that the auction sale was acted upon and that the possession was given to the plaintiff of Title Suit No. 421 of 1977. It further appears that the appellate Court below did not take into consideration the khatian, rent receipts and exhibits filed by the plaintiff petitioner in Title Suit No. 421 of 1977 in support of their contention. Here it may be mentioned that the trial Court below on proper scrutiny and analysis of evidence adduced by the witnesses of both the parties arrive at a finding that the plaintiff petitioner, was able to prove his possession in the suit land although he has miserably failed to substantiate his contention as to the title to the suit land, but the appellate Court below did not controvert that point nor reversed the findings of the Trial Court on that point. In dismissing, Title Suit No. 421 of 1977, the trial Court discussed the evidence adduced by the witnesses of the defendant opposite party No. I of the present Rule and observed that they are highly interested and partisan witnesses and, as such, the oral testimony of the witnesses were discarded by the trial Court on that account. The appellate Court overlooked this aspect of this case and without adverting to that point only considered the documentary evidence adduced by the opposite party No. I and arrived at a finding that the opposite party No. I has been able to prove his case. It thus appears that the impugned judgment of Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986 suffers from gross illegality and infirmity and that in view of the matter I am of the view that the impugned judgment so far it relates to Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986 cannot be maintained.</u>

13. In the result, the Rule in Civil Revision No. 524 of 1990 is discharged and the Rule in Civil Revision 525 of 1990 is made absolute. The judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court in Title Appeal No. 87 of 1986 are set aside and those of the trial Court are restored and Title Suit No. 421 of 1977 is disposed.

14. In view of the circumstances of the case there will be no order as to costs in respect of both the Rules.

Send down the LCR at once.

End.
